finding: VIRGIL runs the seed and the move in an agent shell (DEC-03, DEC-09), but BR-076 keeps git's prompts for the seed 'because a person runs it', and no rule sets prompts, a time limit, or a retry bound for the move; a stale lease restarts the move with no limit. A move that waits on a credential prompt for a new origin can be killed between the marker and the push. Apply the no-prompt mode and the 30-second limit of BR-076 to every git call of the seed and the move, bound the restarts of the move as BR-072 bounds a claim, and add the move to QS-20 or a sibling scenario.
why_this_severity: The nearest scenario, QS-20, has priority 2, so importance is medium; whether the agent shell hangs or fails on a prompt depends on the credential setup, which nobody has checked, so exposure is uncertain. A hang does not by itself hand out an ID twice; ATAM-0014 covers that consequence.

finding: Only a claim and --plan-seed recognise the marker commit (BR-097). The read of the move has no outcome for a marker or a missing counter, although both occur: two sessions in two worktrees both offer the move at the session start (BR-106 checks only the setting and origin), so the second move reads the first one's marker; and a User who declines the seed keeps the setting without a counter (CIF-G06). init-factory also counts a marker as a seeded counter (BR-105), so fitting.counter_seeded is true while every claim fails. Define the outcome of a move that reads a marker or no counter, and state whether the fitting key treats a marker as seeded.
why_this_severity: The affected scenario, QS-23, has priority 2, so importance is medium; every ordering checked fails loudly and hands out no ID twice, and only the message and the fitting key may mislead, so exposure is uncertain.

finding: A move cut off after a successful push and before the setting is removed leaves C on origin. Until the next session start, a clone of the new origin on another machine can claim there, so origin moves on to a claim commit other than C. The second move then reads OriginHoldsOther and reports a collision, although the move went through; the marker and the setting stay, and every local claim fails until a human acts (CIF-G03). Let the collision message print the key=value lines of both claim commits, so a human sees whether every line on origin is at or above the line of C, and state that check in 6.16.1 and BR-102.
why_this_severity: The outcome is a false collision, which QS-23 (priority 2) covers, so importance is medium; it hands out no ID twice, because the marker keeps every local claim away from C; whether other clones claim inside the window is unknown, so exposure is uncertain.
